questions.question: When a line manager is away, how do we know, and can the manager and their own manager both decide the same request?
questions.why_it_matters: You decided that a manager's own manager can step in when the manager is away. Without a clear rule, requests could be stuck with nobody able to decide, or two managers could decide the same request differently.

options.option: The manager marks themselves away, and only then can their manager decide
options.trade_offs: Clear and auditable, but requests wait if the manager forgets to mark themselves away.

options.option: The manager's own manager can decide at any time, alongside the manager
options.trade_offs: Requests never get stuck, but two people may both act, so the first decision must win and the second person is told.

options.option: The manager's own manager can decide only after a request has waited a set number of days
options.trade_offs: No manual step, but needs an agreed waiting time and delays urgent requests.

questions.question: What should a manager see and do when reviewing a loan request, and how do they find requests waiting for them?
questions.why_it_matters: Approving and declining is the step that turns a request into a loan, but the mockup shows no manager screen at all, so this part of the feature cannot be specified yet.

options.option: A list of requests waiting for the manager, with approve and decline on each request
options.trade_offs: Simple and quick for managers; needs a new manager screen.

options.option: Managers act only from the email they receive
options.trade_offs: Least new screen design, but harder to see everything waiting and relies on email delivery.

options.option: Both a waiting list and links from the email
options.trade_offs: Most convenient, with more to design and build.

questions.question: Who may see a staff member's loan requests and decline reasons, and can someone request equipment for another person?
questions.why_it_matters: Loan records and decline reasons are about individual people, so showing them to the wrong person could expose personal information.

options.option: Staff see only their own requests; managers also see their direct reports' requests
options.trade_offs: Matches the approval rule and keeps data limited; stand-in managers need access to the reports they cover.

options.option: Staff see only their own requests; managers see only requests waiting for their decision
options.trade_offs: Smallest exposure of personal data, but managers cannot look back at past decisions.

options.option: Anyone in the company can see all loans
options.trade_offs: Easy to see what equipment is out, but exposes individuals' decline reasons unless they are hidden.

questions.question: Who can cancel a request and until when, who records that an item has been returned, and what happens if an item is not returned by its end date?
questions.why_it_matters: Each status (pending, approved, declined, cancelled, returned) needs a person or event that sets it. Otherwise statuses appear that nobody can set, and cancelled or returned items may never become free for others.

options.option: Staff can cancel until approved; a manager records the return
options.trade_offs: Clear roles, with managers doing extra work and cancelling after approval needing a manager.

options.option: Staff can cancel any time before the loan starts; a designated equipment owner records the return
options.trade_offs: Flexible for staff, but needs someone named as equipment owner.

options.option: Either staff or their manager can cancel; the manager records the return and overdue items are flagged to the manager
options.trade_offs: Covers overdue items, but adds a flag or email that needs designing.

questions.question: Where does the information about each person's line manager, and that manager's manager, come from?
questions.why_it_matters: Who may approve a request and who is emailed on submission both depend on this, and nothing supplied says where it is held or how changes are reflected.

options.option: Use an existing company system such as an HR system or staff directory
options.trade_offs: Always up to date, but needs access to that system and its owner's agreement.

options.option: Keep the reporting lines inside this feature, maintained by an administrator
options.trade_offs: Self-contained, but someone must keep it current as people move.

options.option: Upload a staff and manager list periodically
options.trade_offs: Simple to build, but can be out of date between uploads.

questions.question: Do staff request a specific item (for example Laptop L-221) or any item of a type, can one request cover several items, and who maintains the list of items?
questions.why_it_matters: The rule that an item cannot be loaned twice for overlapping dates cannot be built until we know what is being booked and who keeps the list correct.

options.option: Specific individual items, one per request, maintained by an administrator
options.trade_offs: Precise tracking of who has what; staff must pick a particular item and an administrator keeps the list.

options.option: Item types (for example Laptop), with the system assigning a free item
options.trade_offs: Easier for staff, but needs a way to assign and track the individual item.

options.option: Item types or items, with several items allowed in one request
options.trade_offs: Convenient for bundles, but approval and availability become more complex.

questions.question: Must a manager give a reason when declining a request, and where do they enter it?
questions.why_it_matters: You said staff see any decline reason. This decides whether declined staff always get an explanation.

options.option: A reason is required
options.trade_offs: Staff always get an explanation, but declining takes slightly longer.

options.option: A reason is optional
options.trade_offs: Quicker for managers, but some declined staff see no explanation.

questions.question: The mockup shows the status 'Requested', but your status list says 'pending'. Which wording should staff see for a request awaiting a decision?
questions.why_it_matters: Staff read this label to know where their request stands, and it should match across the list, emails and specification.

options.option: Use 'Pending' and update the mockup
options.trade_offs: Matches your decided statuses; the design changes.

options.option: Use 'Requested' as the displayed label for the pending state
options.trade_offs: Keeps the mockup as is, but the label differs from the decided status name.

options.option: They are two different states
options.trade_offs: Adds a sixth status that needs its own meaning and rules.

questions.question: After staff submit a request successfully, what should they see?
questions.why_it_matters: The mockup's Submit request button leads nowhere, and staff need to know their request was sent and where to find it.

options.option: A confirmation page that says the request was sent
options.trade_offs: Unmistakable, but one more screen and one more click to get back.

options.option: Return to the loans list with a message and the new request shown as pending
options.trade_offs: Faster, and shows the request in place; the message must be easy to notice.

questions.question: If a request cannot be submitted, what should staff see, and should the details they entered be kept?
questions.why_it_matters: Staff should not have to retype the item and dates if something goes wrong, and should understand what to fix.

options.option: Keep entered values and show each message next to the field it concerns
options.trade_offs: Easiest to fix; non-validation failures such as a server error still need their own general message.

options.option: Clear the form and show one general message
options.trade_offs: Simplest to build, but staff must re-enter everything.

recommendation.option: Keep entered values and show each message next to the field it concerns
recommendation.rationale: The kept finding says to keep entered data and show messages beside their fields when validation fails. It is low confidence and covers validation failure only.
